textbookText: **30 questions per topic (120 total).** Answer key with concept notes at the end.
1. A matrix in which the number of rows equals the number of columns is called: A) A square matrix B) A row matrix C) A column matrix D) A rectangular matrix
2. The identity matrix I is characterized by: A) 1's on the principal diagonal and 0's elsewhere B) All entries equal to 1 C) All entries equal to 0 D) 1's below the diagonal only

3. For two matrices to be added, they must: A) Have the same order (same number of rows and columns) B) Both be square matrices C) Have equal determinants D) Have the same number of rows only, regardless of columns

4. Matrix multiplication AB is defined only when: A) The number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B B) The number of rows of A equals the number of rows of B C) A and B are both square matrices of the same order D) A and B have equal determinants

5. In general, for two matrices A and B (both conformable for multiplication): A) AB ≠ BA in general (matrix multiplication is not commutative) B) AB = BA always C) AB = BA only if both are square matrices D) AB is undefined whenever BA is defined
6. The determinant of a 2×2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] is: A) ad − bc B) ad + bc C) ab − cd D) ac − bd
7. A matrix is called singular if its determinant is: A) Equal to zero B) Equal to one C) A negative number D) Greater than zero

8. The inverse of a matrix A exists only if: A) A is a square matrix and its determinant is non-zero (A is non-singular) B) A is a square matrix with determinant equal to zero C) A is any rectangular matrix D) A has all entries equal
9. The formula for the inverse of a 2×2 matrix A is: A) A⁻¹ = (1/det A) × adjoint of A B) A⁻¹ = det A × adjoint of A C) A⁻¹ = A × det A D) A⁻¹ = adjoint of A only, without dividing by determinant

10. The transpose of a matrix A (denoted Aᵀ) is obtained by: A) Interchanging its rows and columns B) Multiplying each element by −1 C) Reversing the order of rows only D) Taking the reciprocal of each element
11. A symmetric matrix satisfies the condition: A) A = Aᵀ B) A = −Aᵀ C) A × Aᵀ = I always D) det(A) = 0 always
12. A skew-symmetric matrix satisfies: A) Aᵀ = −A, and its diagonal elements must all be zero B) Aᵀ = A C) A² = I D) All entries must be positive
13. Cramer's rule is used to: A) Solve a system of linear equations using determinants B) Find the transpose of a matrix C) Add two matrices together D) Determine whether a matrix is symmetric

14. If |A| (determinant of A) = 0 for the coefficient matrix of a system of linear equations, the system: A) Either has no solution or infinitely many solutions (not a unique solution) B) Always has a unique solution C) Always has no solution, with certainty D) Always has infinitely many solutions, with certainty
15. The order of a matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns is written as: A) 3 × 2 B) 2 × 3 C) 3 + 2 D) 6 (product of rows and columns)

16. Which property holds for determinants when two rows (or columns) of a matrix are identical? A) The determinant equals zero B) The determinant equals one C) The determinant is always positive D) The determinant equals the sum of the diagonal elements
17. If a matrix is multiplied by a scalar k, its determinant (for an n×n matrix) is multiplied by: A) kⁿ B) k C) k² regardless of matrix size D) The determinant remains unchanged

18. An extraordinary real-world use of matrices is in: A) Computer graphics, where transformation matrices rotate, scale, and translate images/3D objects B) Only in pure abstract mathematics, with no practical application C) Cooking recipe scaling exclusively D) Measuring temperature only
19. det(AB) for two square matrices A and B of the same order equals: A) det(A) × det(B) B) det(A) + det(B) C) det(A) − det(B) D) det(A)/det(B) always
20. A null (zero) matrix is one in which: A) Every element is zero B) Every element is one C) Only the diagonal elements are zero D) The determinant is always one

21. Solving the system 2x + 3y = 5 and x − y = 1 using matrices means expressing it as: A) AX = B, where A is the coefficient matrix, X the variable matrix, B the constant matrix B) A = X × B always C) X = A + B D) B = A − X

22. The adjoint (adjugate) of a square matrix A is: A) The transpose of the cofactor matrix of A B) The same as the determinant of A C) The inverse of A directly, without any further operation D) Simply A multiplied by −1

23. Which of these is an elementary row operation used in solving matrices? A) Interchanging two rows B) Multiplying the whole matrix by another matrix C) Taking the determinant of a row D) Squaring every element of a row

24. If A is a 3×3 matrix, the minor of an element is obtained by: A) Deleting the row and column containing that element and finding the determinant of the remaining 2×2 matrix B) Multiplying the element by its row number C) Adding all elements of that row D) Finding the transpose of the whole matrix
